name: Bank of Baroda
title: Bank of Baroda - 532134 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Bank of Baroda Q4 FY26 net profit rose 11.2% YoY to a record Rs 5,616 crore; FY26 net profit Rs 20,021 crore, with FY27 loan growth guidance raised to 12-14%.
summary.overview: Global business crossed Rs 30 lakh crore at Rs 30.78 lakh crore (+13.9% YoY), with global advances up 16.2% and total deposits up 12%. Q4 operating profit was Rs 9,069 crore (+11.5% YoY) and NII grew 8.7%, with NIM at 2.89% (+10 bps QoQ) helped partly by interest on income-tax refunds. Asset quality improved (GNPA 1.89%, net NPA 0.45%), but Q4 credit cost rose to 0.76% after a Rs 1,500 crore floating provision funded from IT refunds. Management raised FY27 loan and deposit growth guidance and set a Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 raise plan, while cautioning that cost of deposits will stay sticky in Q1 given tight liquidity and West Asia tensions.

financial_highlights.value: 0.76% (0.32% excluding Rs 1,500 crore floating provision); FY26 0.46% (0.34% excluding floating provision)

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Organic retail book grew 17.9% YoY and crossed Rs 3 lakh crore; auto loans +20.6%, mortgages +19.3%, home loans +14.6%, education +10.9%, personal loans +8.7%. RAM share of advances is 61%.

segments.name: Agriculture and MSME
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 20.7% and organic MSME 15.6%. MSME book is about Rs 1.6 lakh crore, of which 55-60% is working capital; ECLGS disbursement estimated at Rs 12,000 crore plus.

segments.name: Corporate and international
segments.commentary: Corporate loans grew 11.2% YoY. International advances grew 24.4%; US operations are about 37-38% of the international book. Management says Middle East exposure is about Rs 50,000-60,000 crore across multiple countries, with no asset-quality impact yet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan growth guidance raised to 12-14% from 11-13%.
FY27 deposit growth guidance raised to 10-12% from 9-11%.
FY27 NIM guidance 2.75-2.95%, which management says includes volatility from IT refund interest; management said it would not breach 2.75% over the four quarters.
ROA guidance kept at more than 1%; slippage ratio kept at 1-1.25%; full-year credit cost guided below 0.60%.
Normalised recoveries from written-off accounts guided at Rs 750-800 crore; management said Q4 recovery was higher than guidance.
Cost of deposits expected to stay sticky in Q1 FY27 given tight liquidity. Management sees scope to reprice MCLR-linked assets; MCLR is 36% and repo-linked 35% of the book.
Hiring of 4,000-5,000 headcount in FY27, against a plan of 6,000-7,000.
capex_capacity: Capital plan: Rs 6,000 crore of AT-1/Tier 2 in FY27, with no fixed timeline and execution depending on pricing. An enabling Rs 8,500 crore equity raise runs through FY28.
Tech spend (opex plus capex) was about Rs 4,500 crore; management says it is adequately covered, with extra spend possible if needed. Tech spend is about 10% of operating profit as a norm.

New subsidiaries: BOB Securities and Gilt Edge Ltd (primary dealer, operational from 1 April 2026, Rs 2,000 crore capital committed, Rs 500 crore availed); pension fund sponsorship approval received, with 6-9 months expected to launch.
Green infrastructure bond of Rs 10,000 crore raised, 3x subscribed; green deposits of Rs 1,899 crore.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth of 12% outpaced by the 16.2% advances growth, a gap management views as sustainable given excess SLR and bulk deposit usage.
Bulk deposits rose to 19% of total deposits in March from 17% a couple of quarters earlier; management says it will stay below 20%.
Domestic SLR is about 22.5-23%, roughly 4.5-5% above the statutory level; management targets 3-3.5% excess SLR.
Collection efficiency excluding agriculture is 98.9%, up from December. CRILC SMA-1 and 2 fell to 0.18% from 0.33% a year earlier.
Management said MSME stress (SMA-0 to SMA-2) was better in March than December, and auto loan stress remains very small.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 NIM improvement came from IT refund interest, and how much is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number and said it is a recurring but volatile line item (about Rs 100 crore to interest income in Q4 per a later reply). It treats the 2.89% as core and the 2.75-2.95% range as covering refund volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,500 crore floating provision linked to ECL or West Asia?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a balance-sheet buffer funded by IT refunds, aimed at lifting PCR and keeping net NPA low. It cannot be used without regulatory approval and is separate from ECL. ECL impact is not yet quantified; management said it should be broadly in line with earlier estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Why was loan guidance raised after a 16.2% growth year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth has been strong since 31 March on a daily YoY basis, the deposit base is recovering, and it expects the geopolitical disruption may not last long. It raised guidance by 1 percentage point.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of deposits outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits (4.78% total, 4.99% domestic) is expected to stay sticky for at least the next three months as liquidity remains tight; management does not expect further reductions and sees repricing mainly on the asset side.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to the Middle East and overseas book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Middle East exposure at about Rs 50,000-60,000 crore across multiple countries, some A-rated, with US about 37-38% of the international book. Trade is below 20% of overseas exposure, and no asset-quality impact has been seen yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for agriculture and the weak monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Agriculture GNPA fell year on year. Fresh slippages are normal and were offset by recoveries. Management does not expect a weak monsoon to materially affect the portfolio.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: a prolonged war or high oil prices could affect the overseas book, Middle East operations and MSME borrowers; management is watching this closely over the next couple of quarters.
Cost of deposits is sticky and asset repricing is still to be shown; NIM guidance of 2.75-2.95% relies partly on volatile IT refund interest.
ECL implementation: quantification is pending, with management indicating it will show up in the books from the first quarter of implementation.
Credit cost run rate is guided below 0.60%, but the Q4 level of 0.76% included the one-time floating provision.
Bulk deposit share, LCR (about 127%), and the timing and pricing of the Rs 6,000 crore AT-1/Tier 2 issuance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, profitability and asset quality, with several guidance upgrades. Cautious and hedged on margin, deposit costs and West Asia exposure, repeatedly saying impacts are unquantified and depend on liquidity and the conflict's duration. Evasive on ECL quantum and bilateral accounts such as Vodafone Idea.
key_quotes: So, in terms of customer income, we have improved, the NIM has improved vis-a-vis the last quarter from 2.79% to 2.89% with the domestic NIM at 3.04%.
The credit cost for the full year is going to be less than 0.60%.
I'm not predicting any increase in deposit rate.
Our floating provision cannot be used without the regulatory approval and that can only be used on extraordinary scenarios.

growth.why: FY27 loan growth guidance raised to 12-14% (from 11-13%) and deposit growth to 10-12%, backed by advances growth of 16.2% and deposits of 12% in FY26 plus excess SLR and bulk deposits, but no specific capacity or order book was quantified.
